public_rationale: There was meaningful evidence before the post: Salesforce attributed reduced engineering hiring to AI, SignalFire documented weaker graduate hiring, and a published study found reduced novice freelance demand in AI-complementary skill groups. None cleanly identifies AI-caused losses of entry-level software engineering positions while addressing the stated alternatives. These findings prevent treating the claim as established merely because a perfectly matched study was not found, but they also fall short of a decisive contradiction under the narrower reading of proof.
limitations: The Salesforce evidence is an executive statement reported by news media.
Graduate hiring and novice freelance postings are imperfect measures of entry-level engineering employment.
Later publications cannot settle what proof was public when the post appeared.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: There is not yet proof that AI is taking entry-level software engineering jobs, as opposed to, for example, outsourcing.

statement.excerpt: there’s yet to be proof it’s actually happening, or that AI’s taking these jobs and not, say, outsourcing.

our_interpretation: This is a claim about what had been established publicly by June 16, 2025, not a claim that later research could never find displacement.
Proof means credible causal evidence or a verified company case specific to entry-level software engineering.
Lost opportunities can include reduced hiring, but this must be distinguished from layoffs and from reduced demand for individual freelance tasks.
The target is the accumulated evidence record through publication, so no starting date is supplied.
Studies published after the post cannot retroactively become proof available when it was written.
criteria.support_condition: A sufficiently comprehensive review of the contemporaneous record establishes that entry-level engineering displacement had not been credibly attributed to AI after considering alternative explanations.
criteria.contradiction_condition: At least one study or verified case public by the post credibly attributes lost entry-level engineering jobs or hiring opportunities to AI, addressing plausible competing explanations.

evidence.publisher: Bloomberg, republished by The Business Times
evidence.explanation: This is a contemporaneous executive attribution of reduced engineering hiring to AI, rather than merely a future forecast. It supplies no entry-level breakdown or independently verified comparison addressing other causes.

The report documents declining new-graduate hiring but discusses financing conditions and previous overhiring alongside AI. Its descriptive data do not isolate an AI effect on entry-level software engineering.

evidence.locator: Introduction; see also section 3.2.2 and Table 2
evidence.publisher: Journal of Economic Behavior & Organization; Oxford repository
evidence.explanation: The study uses comparisons over time and between exposure groups to examine freelance demand, including a novice-worker decline in a broad category containing programming skills. It does not separately establish lost entry-level software engineering positions; employer-requested experience is also not the actual experience of hired workers.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A study or independently verified company case available by June 16, 2025 that identifies entry-level engineering opportunities lost to AI and credibly addresses outsourcing, financing conditions and other competing explanations.
